newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-Council parliament sends team to Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: Euro-Council parliament sends team to Belgrade.

text.p: The Council of Europe Parliamentary Assembly said on Monday it was sending a delegation to Belgrade as anti-government protests over alleged electoral fraud entered their fifth week.

"The purpose is to get first-hand information on the crisis, to encourage the forces of genuine democracy and to prepare for a debate at the next plenary session of the assembly in January 1997," the assembly said in a statement.
The 40-nation council was established after World War Two to promote democracy and human rights in Europe.
Opposition supporters and students in Yugoslavia have protested since mid-November at the alleged electoral fraud.

The demonstrations have shaken socialist President Slobodan Milosevic and given the United States a fresh opportunity to press him for democratic reform in Serbia in return for renewed access to international financial institutions.
